name: Beraiah
overview: Beraiah is a male figure from the tribe of Benjamin, identified uniquely as the son of Shimei according to 1 Chronicles 8:21. There are no additional notes or details provided about his life or role in Scripture beyond this familial connection.
namesAndTitles: The name Beraiah means 'YHWH has created,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning rooted in the Hebrew language. This proper name is not indicated to have been given directly by God but carries a significant declaration of divine creation as understood in the Old Testament context.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Beraiah as the son of Shema, establishing a direct paternal relationship. Beyond this, no further family relationships are documented in the biblical text provided.
scriptureSignificance: Beraiah's significance lies primarily in his genealogical mention within the tribe of Benjamin, marking him as part of the covenant people of God. His identification as the son of Shimei situates him within the broader narrative of Israel's tribal lineage, which is foundational for understanding God's unfolding plan through His chosen people. Although details about his personal actions are not recorded, his inclusion in the genealogical record underscores the importance of lineage and heritage in the biblical narrative.
